scenes.display: IRIV IO Controller + Wilcoxon 883M, analysed by Viking Analytics.
scenes.text: This vibration monitor uses an IRIV IO Controller, running the Wilcoxon gateway firmware. It reads a Wilcoxon eight eight three M, and publishes to Viking Analytics over MQTT.
The sensor measures. The controller polls it and publishes. Viking Analytics learns the machine, and flags what changes.

segments.text: The eight eight three M sits on the motor, and measures vibration on three axes, plus temperature.
The controller polls it over Modbus, and publishes each reading as MQTT.
MultiViz learns what normal looks like.

scenes.text: The Wilcoxon eight eight three M measures vibration in X, Y and Z, plus temperature. It reports acceleration, velocity and displacement, along with waveforms and a frequency spectrum. Its acceleration range is plus or minus sixteen g, with a frequency response from two hertz to five kilohertz. The compact housing is thirty five millimetres wide and twenty six millimetres high, with an M eight connector. It sends digital readings over Modbus R T U. These measurements help track changes in a machine; diagnosis also needs its operating conditions and history.

scenes.display: 883M A and B to RS485 A and B, ground to G. Terminator on.
scenes.text: Its RS485 pair lands on A and B, with ground on G. The controller ends the bus, so the terminator switch goes on.

scenes.display: One 24 V DC rail for the controller and the sensor.
scenes.text: A twenty four volt supply powers the controller, and the sensor shares the same rail.
Install the firmware from the web installer. Then set the MQTT broker and the alarm limits in the controller's own web dashboard.
MultiViz learns a baseline for each sensor, so there are no thresholds to tune. When the pattern shifts, it names the symptom, and ranks which machine needs attention first.

scenes.display: DO0 follows the dashboard alarm, latched. The relay contact runs the beacon.
scenes.text: Now the alarm. Output zero follows the dashboard alarm, and drives a twenty four volt relay for a beacon and buzzer.

scenes.display: DI1: acknowledge push button. DI0: start a capture.
scenes.text: A push button on input one acknowledges the alarm. Input zero can start a capture.

segments.text: Vibration on the motor climbs past the alarm limit.
After the delay, the controller trips the alarm. Output zero closes the relay, and the beacon flashes.
The operator presses acknowledge. While vibration is still high, the relay stays on.
Once it clears, the relay drops, and the alarm is ready again.

scenes.text: The rule runs on the controller. Trip on velocity or temperature, after a delay, and latch the relay. It drops only when the alarm is acknowledged, and the reading has cleared.
Sense, analyse, act. One sensor, one controller, and an alarm that someone has to answer.
